source_refs.note: Exercise 2.7, Question 3 (book page 70). The book prints no answers for Unit 2; results verified with sympy.

blocks.prompt: 3. A closed cylindrical tank is to be constructed to hold \(54\pi\) liters of water. Find the dimensions that minimize the construction cost of the tank.
blocks.explanation:
A minimum problem: least cost means least sheet metal, i.e. least total surface area.
Given: the volume \(54\pi\) litres \(= 54\pi\text{ dm}^{3}\). To find: radius and height.
Plan: use the volume to write \(h\) in terms of \(r\), minimize \(S = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh\), and give the answer in dm and cm.
steps:
Given: a closed cylinder holding \(54\pi\) litres.
To find: the radius \(r\) and height \(h\) for least construction cost.
Method: assume each square unit of metal costs the same, so the cost is least when the total surface area (two ends + curved surface) is least. Then the derivative tests.

Units
\[1\text{ litre} = 1\text{ dm}^{3}\]
\[V = 54\pi\text{ dm}^{3}\]
Why: working in decimetres keeps the numbers small; we convert to cm at the end.

Constraint (volume)
\[\pi r^{2}h = 54\pi\]
\[h = \dfrac{54}{r^{2}} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Why: the volume is fixed, so it links \(h\) to \(r\).

Surface area in one variable
\[S = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi rh \quad \text{...(2)}\]
\[S = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi r\cdot\dfrac{54}{r^{2}}\]
\[S = 2\pi r^{2} + \dfrac{108\pi}{r}\]
Why: a closed tank has a top and a bottom (\(2\pi r^{2}\)) and a curved surface (\(2\pi rh\)).

Critical point
\[\dfrac{dS}{dr} = 4\pi r - \dfrac{108\pi}{r^{2}} \quad \text{...(3)}\]
\[4\pi r = \dfrac{108\pi}{r^{2}} \Rightarrow r^{3} = 27\]
\[r = 3\text{ dm}\]
Why: \(\frac{108\pi}{r} = 108\pi r^{-1}\) has derivative \(-108\pi r^{-2}\); cancel \(4\pi\): \(r^{3} = \frac{108}{4} = 27\).

Second derivative test
\[\dfrac{d^{2}S}{dr^{2}} = 4\pi + \dfrac{216\pi}{r^{3}}\]
\[\text{At } r = 3: \ 4\pi + 8\pi = 12\pi > 0\]
Why: positive, so \(S\) (and the cost) is minimum at \(r = 3\) dm.

Height and check
\[h = \dfrac{54}{3^{2}} = 6\text{ dm}\]
\[S_{\min} = 18\pi + 36\pi = 54\pi\text{ dm}^{2}\]
\[\pi(3)^{2}(6) = 54\pi\ \checkmark\]
Why: from (1). The height equals the diameter (\(h = 2r\)), as always for a closed cylinder of least surface area (compare Example 32).
blocks.final_answer: Radius \(r = 3\) dm \(= 30\) cm and height \(h = 6\) dm \(= 60\) cm (height = diameter); least surface area \(54\pi\text{ dm}^{2} \approx 1.70\text{ m}^{2}\).
